description.value: A self-sufficient wilderness park on a chain of lakes and wetlands in the upper Emar Creek watershed, with user-maintained campsites at Janice and Willowgrouse Lakes; no potable water and an unmarked entrance off Hwy 24.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms this is an operational, free, user-maintained wilderness campsite with capacity 5. The website explicitly states 'potable water is not available in the park,' confirming that amenity false. No other amenities (showers, reservations, charging, etc.) are mentioned; the site is described as a remote, self-sufficient wilderness area primarily oriented around a canoe route, with no cycling-specific infrastructure noted anywhere in the content.
concerns: No address or phone number in OSM record.
Access directions on website describe driving to the park entrance — no indication of bikeable access route.
Park is described as wilderness, not regularly serviced or patrolled; very limited capacity (5 spots) and no amenities beyond primitive camping.
Primary use case appears to be canoe touring, not bicycle touring.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a remote, free, user-maintained wilderness campsite (capacity 5) primarily oriented toward canoeists; the approach directions reference driving, no cycling infrastructure or hiker/biker designation is mentioned, and the lack of any facilities (no water, no services) may not meet WWC utility thresholds for touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: Fee is confirmed free (OSM fee=no; BC Parks website does not mention any camping fee for this park). Internet access confirmed absent (OSM internet_access=no).

wow_evidence: potable water is not available in the park
